title: Etale local finite restriction of a closed affine relation
statement: Let $T,U,R$ be affine schemes [def-pc-scheme]. Let $U\to T$ be locally quasi-finite [pqf-def-quasifinite], and let $s,t:R\to U$ be etale morphisms over $T$ [def-weil-etale-morphism]. Suppose $j=(s,t):R\to U\times_TU$ is a closed immersion [def-pc-fibre-product, def-weil-closed-immersion] identifying $R(H)$ with an equivalence relation on $U(H)$ for every $T$-scheme $H$. For every $u\in U$, with image $p\in T$, there exist an affine scheme $T'$, an etale map $T'\to T$, a point $p'\in T'$ over $p$ inducing an isomorphism of residue fields [def-weil-residue-field], and decompositions into open and closed subschemes $U\times_TT'=U'\amalg W$, $R\times_TT'=R'\amalg W'$, with a point $u'\in U'$ over both $u$ and $p'$, such that $U'$ and $R'$ are finite over $T'$ [def-weil-finite-integral-morphism] and $R'=U'\times_{U\times_TT',s}(R\times_TT')\times_{t,U\times_TT'}U'$ as a restricted relation. The restricted projections $s',t':R'\to U'$ are etale and form an equivalence relation. Open and closed subschemes have their induced scheme structures [def-weil-open-immersion].

source.place: Tag 03X5 (lemma-quasi-finite-over-base-j-proper), specialized to an affine etale equivalence relation with closed relation map; conclusions (a), (d), (g), (h), with an affine shrinking of the etale neighbourhood.

proof.text: Write $f:U\to T$ for the structure map. It is locally of finite type by [lem-weil-pbc-lqf-locally-finite-type], and separated by [lem-weil-pbc-affine-source-morphism-separated], since $U$ is affine. Local quasi-finiteness means in particular that $f$ is quasi-finite at the chosen $u$. Therefore $u$ is an isolated point of the scheme-theoretic fibre over $p=f(u)$ by [lem-weil-pbc-quasi-finite-at-point-isolated]. These are exactly the hypotheses needed for the isolated-point splitting theorem.

Apply [lem-weil-pbc-etale-splits-off-isolated-points-technical] to $f$, $p$, and the singleton list $(u)$. It gives an elementary etale neighbourhood $(S_1,p_1)\to(T,p)$ and a decomposition $U\times_TS_1=V\amalg W_1$ into open and closed subschemes with $V\to S_1$ finite and a point $v\in V$ over both $u$ and $p_1$. In particular the induced map $\kappa(p)\to\kappa(p_1)$ is an isomorphism. The order of the fibre-product factors is changed using the universal property [def-pc-fibre-product].

Choose an affine open neighbourhood $T'\subseteq S_1$ of $p_1$ and denote the same point by $p'$. Its inclusion is etale, so $T'\to T$ is etale by [lem-weil-pbc-etale-composition-cancellation]. The residue field at a point is unchanged on an open subscheme [def-weil-open-immersion], hence $\kappa(p)\to\kappa(p')$ is still an isomorphism. Pulling back the decomposition gives $U\times_TT'=U'\amalg W$, where $U'=V\times_{S_1}T'$ is finite by [lem-weil-pbc-finite-morphism-permanence](a). The point $v$ lies in this inverse image and gives $u'\in U'$ over $u$ and $p'$. The open neighbourhood exists because schemes are locally affine [def-pc-scheme].

source.place: Tag 02LN, restriction to an affine neighbourhood; morphisms.tex Tags 01WL (lemma-base-change-finite), 02GP (lemma-open-immersion-etale), 02GN (lemma-composition-etale)

proof.text: Apply [lem-a1-clopen-relation-base-change-identification] to the given relation, $B=T'$, and $V=U'$. It gives the clopen decomposition $R\times_TT'=R'\amalg W'$, the required iterated fibre-product identification, and the equivalence-relation assertion for the two induced projections on every $T'$-scheme. Here the base-changed endpoint maps are used, so all points and relation axioms are relative to the same fixed map to $T'$.

source.place: Tag 02VD (lemma-restrict-groupoid-relation), with arbitrary base change and the induced clopen open-subscheme realization; specialization used in more-groupoids.tex Tag 03X5 (lemma-quasi-finite-over-base-j-proper), conclusion (h).

proof.text: Apply [lem-a1-finite-clopen-relation-projection-properties] with $B=T'$ and the finite clopen piece $V=U'$ of step 3. Its hypotheses are precisely the assumed closed immersion $j$ and etale maps $s,t$. The identification in step 4 commutes with both endpoint maps; hence the two statements concern the same restricted projections. Thus it makes $R'$ finite over $T'$ and its two restricted projections etale. Together with $u'$ and the residue-field isomorphism from step 3, these are all the required conclusions.

source.place: Tag 03X5 (lemma-quasi-finite-over-base-j-proper), closed-immersion specialization of the restricted-relation argument and finiteness of the object square; etale projection permanence as in the preceding lemma-quasi-finite-over-base.

proof_origin.place: Tag 03X5, specialized argument using Tag 02LN (more-morphisms.tex). Since j is a closed immersion, any finite clopen U-piece yields a finite restricted relation; the orbit and shrinking argument required by the general universally closed case is unnecessary for the conclusions of this item.

lean.statement: theorem exists_finite_etale_restricted_relation_neighbourhood {T U R : Scheme.{u}} [IsAffine T] [IsAffine U] [IsAffine R] (fU : U ⟶ T) (fR : R ⟶ T) (hquasi : Scheme.Hom.IsLocallyQuasiFinite fU) (s t : R ⟶ U) (hs : s ≫ fU = fR) (ht : t ≫ fU = fR) (hsEtale : Etale s) (htEtale : Etale t) (j : R ⟶ pullback fU fU) (hj_s : j ≫ pullback.fst fU fU = s) (hj_t : j ≫ pullback.snd fU fU = t) (hj_closed : IsClosedImmersion j) (hrel : ∀ (H : Scheme.{u}) (hH : H ⟶ T), _root_.Equivalence (fun (a b : {g : H ⟶ U // g ≫ fU = hH}) => ∃ r : H ⟶ R, r ≫ s = a.1 ∧ r ≫ t = b.1)) (u : U) : let p : T := fU u ∃ (T' : Scheme.{u}) (f' : T' ⟶ T) (p' : T'), IsAffine T' ∧ Etale f' ∧ f' p' = p ∧ IsIso (f'.residueFieldMap p') ∧ ∃ (Uo Wo : (pullback fU f').Opens), IsCompl Uo Wo ∧ ∃ (u' : Uo.toScheme), pullback.fst fU f' (Uo.ι u') = u ∧ pullback.snd fU f' (Uo.ι u') = p' ∧ IsFinite (Uo.ι ≫ pullback.snd fU f') ∧ ∃ (Ro Wro : (pullback fR f').Opens), IsCompl Ro Wro ∧ IsFinite (Ro.ι ≫ pullback.snd fR f') ∧ let U0 := pullback fU f' let R0 := pullback fR f' let s0 : R0 ⟶ U0 := pullback.map fR f' fU f' s (𝟙 T') (𝟙 T) (by simpa using hs.symm) (by simp) let t0 : R0 ⟶ U0 := pullback.map fR f' fU f' t (𝟙 T') (𝟙 T) (by simpa using ht.symm) (by simp) let P := pullback Uo.ι s0 let Q := pullback (pullback.snd Uo.ι s0 ≫ t0) Uo.ι let p₁ := pullback.fst Uo.ι s0 let p₂ := pullback.snd Uo.ι s0 let q₁ := pullback.fst (pullback.snd Uo.ι s0 ≫ t0) Uo.ι let q₂ := pullback.snd (pullback.snd Uo.ι s0 ≫ t0) Uo.ι ∃ (q : Ro.toScheme ⟶ Q), IsIso q ∧ q ≫ q₁ ≫ p₂ = Ro.ι ∧ Ro.ι ≫ s0 = (q ≫ q₁ ≫ p₁) ≫ Uo.ι ∧ Ro.ι ≫ t0 = (q ≫ q₂) ≫ Uo.ι ∧ Etale (q ≫ q₁ ≫ p₁) ∧ Etale (q ≫ q₂) ∧ ∀ (H : Scheme.{u}) (hH : H ⟶ T'), _root_.Equivalence (fun (a b : {g : H ⟶ Uo.toScheme // g ≫ (Uo.ι ≫ pullback.snd fU f') = hH}) => ∃ r : H ⟶ Ro.toScheme, r ≫ (q ≫ q₁ ≫ p₁) = a.1 ∧ r ≫ (q ≫ q₂) = b.1)
